tip: 'yağarken' means while it rains. Adding '-ken' to the aorist 'yağar' builds a while-doing clause running alongside the main action.
'babanın arabası' means father's car. The owner takes '-nın' and the thing owned takes '-sı', so both ends of the pair are marked.
'ya otobüse bineriz ya da yürürüz' means either we take the bus or we walk. The frame 'ya ... ya da' sets up the two choices.
'ödemiş olacağım' means I will have paid. The '-mış' form plus 'olacağım' places the action as finished by a future point.
'olacağını' means that there will be, as the object of 'haber verdi'. The '-acağını' ending packs a whole future clause into one word ending in the object marker.
'büyümeye devam ediyor' means keeps growing. 'devam etmek' needs the '-e' ending on the verbal noun, so 'büyüme' becomes 'büyümeye'.
To report a command, add '-me' plus a possessive and '-i' to the verb: 'giymemi söyledi' means told me to wear.
Add '-ken' to a verb to mean while doing it: 'geçerken' means while passing.
'binmek' takes the '-a' ending for what you board: 'uçağa bindim' means I got on the plane.
The '-ş' in 'vedalaştık' marks a mutual action: we said goodbye to each other, not one-way.
Possession takes two endings, '-un' on the owner and '-si' on the thing: 'okulun bahçesi' means the school's garden.
'-seydin' plus '-erdim' makes an unreal past: 'söyleseydin yardım ederdim' means if you had told me, I would have helped.
The '-miş' in 'dağılmış' shows an inferred result: the toys are scattered, noticed after the fact, not watched happening.
For when I do something, add '-dığım' plus '-da' to the verb: 'anımsadığımda' means when I remember.
The aorist plus 'mu' makes a polite request: 'konuşur musunuz' means would you please speak.
'-ul' makes this verb passive: 'konuşmak' is to speak, 'konuşulur' means is spoken.
'hem ... hem de' links two facts as both and: 'hem gezdi hem de aldı' means both wandered and bought.
'karar vermek' needs the '-maya' form of the next verb: 'kurmaya karar verdi' means decided to start.
'gidemeyecek kadar yoğundu' means too busy to go: 'gidemeyecek' is cannot go and 'kadar' marks the degree, giving a too X to do reading.
Position words like 'arkasında' (behind) mark the noun as the possessor: 'caminin arkasında' means at the back of the mosque.
For reported speech the verb takes '-eceğini': 'geleceğini' means that she would come, followed by 'söyledi' (said).
Here 'yeni' means just or recently, not new: 'yeni yürümeyi öğrendi' means has just learned to walk.
The suffix '-ince' means when or once something happens: 'esince' means when it blew.
Passive uses 'edildi' (was done) with a noun: 'inşa edildi' means was built, and no doer is named.
Nouns pair with 'yapmak' (to do) to form verbs: 'spor yapıyorum' means I do sport, that is I exercise.
Add '-ki' to make a possessive pronoun: 'seninki' means yours, and 'seninkini' adds the object ending '-ni'.
The suffix '-ken' means while: 'yağarken' means while it was raining, marking two things happening at once.
Comparisons use '-den' plus 'daha': 'ötekinden daha ilginç' means more interesting than the other one.
For after doing something use '-tıktan sonra': 'yaptıktan sonra' means after doing it.
To name the doer in a passive, use 'tarafından' (by): 'binlerce kişi tarafından' means by thousands of people.
